title: How a rabbit study and an ex-student boost my hopes for a future of 'love and dignity' ｜ 一项兔子研究与前学生如何让我对未来"爱与尊严"充满希望

sents.en: At whatever grade level teachers find themselves, from kindergarten to the final class at medical or law school, few moments stir the emotions as deeply as when former students reappear years and often decades later with an update on where their journey has taken them and what resiliencies have been the pavement on which they've traveled.
sents.cn: 无论教师身处何种年级层次，从幼儿园到医学院或法学院的最后一课，很少有哪个时刻能像当年学生多年乃至数十年后再次出现、讲述他们人生旅程去向何方、以及何种韧性铺就了他们前行之路时那样，深深触动情感。

sents.en: So it was when a recent letter came from Kelli Harding, a student 21 years ago in my Peace Studies summer course in Washington.
sents.cn: 最近收到凯莉∙哈丁的来信便是如此。

sents.en: The weekly tuition-free class, in a roomy space that Ralph Nader and his Public Citizen nonprofit group provided, was discussion-based and required no useless homework or exams.
sents.cn: 她是21年前我在华盛顿"和平研究"暑期课程的学生。

sents.en: Just come in and figure out how to increase peace and decrease violence.
sents.cn: 这门每周一次、免学费的课程，由拉尔夫∙纳德及其"公共公民"非营利组织提供宽敞场地，以讨论为主，无需无用的家庭作业或考试。

sents.en: And do it today, tomorrow is too late.
sents.cn: 只需走进来，思考如何增进和平、减少暴力——而且要今天行动，明天就太迟了。

sents.en: The course attracted mostly congressional interns, with a few exceptions like Kelli who was in Washington as an AmeriCorps volunteer.
sents.cn: 课程吸引的大多是国会实习生，也有少数例外，比如作为"美国志愿队"志愿者在华盛顿的凯莉。

sents.en: Her year-long service included comforting AIDs patients at a free health clinic and delivering meals to the homebound.
sents.cn: 她为期一年的服务包括在一家免费诊所安抚艾滋病患者，并为居家不便者送餐。

sents.en: It was a world apart from her undergraduate days at the University of California-Berkeley majoring in political science.
sents.cn: 这与她在加州大学伯克利分校攻读政治学的本科时光截然不同。

sents.en: The Washington experience, which Kelli would later call transformative, was the fuel that carried her into medicine to earn a master's degree in public health from Columbia University and a medical degree from the University of Rochester, and almost two decades of practice as an emergency-room psychiatrist at New York-Presbyterian Hospital and a clinical professor of psychiatry at Columbia University Irving Medical Center.
sents.cn: 这段华盛顿经历——凯莉后来称之为"改变人生"——成为动力，推动她投身医学，取得哥伦比亚大学公共卫生硕士学位和罗切斯特大学医学学位，并在纽约-长老会医院担任急诊精神科医生近二十年，同时是哥伦比亚大学欧文医学中心的临床精神病学教授。

sents.en: Kelli's letter, a literate update on both her personal and professional life, touched my heart, and especially so when saying that two decades later she still has the course text, "Solutions to Violence," and that "it remains one of my favorite possessions." She lives in Lower Manhattan with her husband, Padraic, whom she met on a flight to London, and their three boys.
sents.cn: 凯莉的来信，对她个人与职业生涯做了颇具文采的更新，深深打动了我的心；尤其是她提到，二十年后她仍保留着课程教材《化解暴力》，并说"它仍是我最珍爱的物品之一"。她与丈夫帕德里克（两人在飞往伦敦的航班上相识）及三个儿子住在曼哈顿下城。

sents.en: If Kelli stands out, it's because she is also a gifted writer.
sents.cn: 如果说凯莉出类拔萃，那是因为她也是一位天赋异禀的作家。

sents.en: Last month, Atria Books published her book The Rabbit Effect: Live Longer, Happier, and Healthier with the Groundbreaking Science of Kindness.
sents.cn: 上个月，阿特里亚出版社推出了她的著作《兔子效应：用开创性的善意科学活得更长久、更快乐、更健康》。

sents.en: With a blending of free-flowing confessional prose and scholarly research found in 461 notes, Kelli met my expectations that her ideas and ideals would be sound and singular.
sents.cn: 凭借流畅的自白式散文与461条注释中的学术研究相结合，凯莉印证了我对她思想与理想的期待——既可靠又独到。

sents.en: "Despite our scientific progress," she writes, "Americans are remarkably unhealthy.
sents.cn: 她写道："尽管我们在科学上取得了进步，美国人却出奇地不健康。

sents.en: In 2016, the United States ranked forty-third in the world for life expectancy....
sents.cn: 2016年，美国在预期寿命上排名世界第四十三位……它也是迄今为止生病代价最昂贵的地方。

sents.en: It is also by far the world's most expensive place to get sick."

Enter the rabbits·not those running around in our woodlands but ones serving in two month-long medical experiments to test the effects of eating a high-fat diet and the connections between cholesterol and heart disease.
sents.cn: 接下来说说兔子——不是林间奔跑的那些，而是参加两项为期一个月的医学实验的兔子，实验旨在测试高脂饮食的影响，以及胆固醇与心脏病之间的关联。

sents.en: With similar diets, the expectations were that all the rabbits would have similar cloggings of their arteries.
sents.cn: 在饮食相似的情况下，预期所有兔子都会出现类似的动脉堵塞。

sents.en: Yet one group had 60% fewer of them.
sents.cn: 然而其中一组的堵塞却少了60%。

sents.en: The reason?
sents.cn: 原因何在？

sents.en: Instead of receiving the standard care given to lab animals, the 60% group was watched over by a newcomer to the lab who, Kelli writes, "handled the animals differently.
sents.cn: 那组减少60%的兔子没有接受实验动物标准照料，而是由实验室的一名新人照看。

sents.en: When she fed her rabbits she talked to them and petted them.
sents.cn: 凯莉写道："她对待动物的方式不同。

sents.en: She didn't just pass out food, she gave them love...
sents.cn: 喂食时她和兔子说话、抚摸它们。

sents.en: The studies indicate something is missing in the traditional biomedical model.
sents.cn: 她不只是分发食物，而是给予它们爱……这些研究表明，传统生物医学模式遗漏了某些东西。

sents.en: It wasn't diet or genetics that made a difference in which rabbits got sick and which stayed healthy.
sents.cn: 让兔子患病与否产生差异的，不是饮食或基因，而是善意。

sents.en: It was kindness."

Amid the political noise about Obamacare, Medicare, Medicaid, health insurance and thieving pharmaceutical companies, Kelli Harding stands apart from the crowd calling for quick fixes, the simpler the better.
sents.cn: 在关于奥巴马医改、联邦医保、医疗补助、健康保险和贪婪制药公司的政治喧嚣中，凯莉∙哈丁脱离了那些呼吁速效方案、越简单越好的群体。

sents.en: She has walked too many miles in the halls of hospitals visiting too many far-gone patients and seeing too many medical mistakes to go along with conventional thinking.
sents.cn: 她在医院走廊里走过的路太长，探望过的晚期病人太多，见过的医疗失误太多，无法认同传统思维。

sents.en: "The rabbit effect," she explains, means that "when it comes to our health, we've been missing some crucial pieces: hidden factors behind what really makes us healthy.
sents.cn: 她解释说，"兔子效应"意味着"在健康问题上，我们一直遗漏了一些关键部分：真正让我们健康的隐藏因素。诸如爱、友谊和尊严之类的因素。我们社区、学校和职场的设计。健康存在一个社会维度，而我们在追求最好、最前沿的医疗时完全忽视了它……归根结底，以最有意义的方式影响我们健康的，更多关乎我们如何对待彼此、如何生活、以及如何思考'做人'的意义，而非诊所里发生的任何事。"K)Inmorethanafewpassages,sherelatesthestoriesofmenandwomenwhocameupagainstassembly-linemedicinewherepatientsweretreatedmostlyaspiecesofflesh."Clinically,"shewrites,"it'scommontoseetwopatientswiththesamecondition,suchasrecoveringfromaheartattack,havetwoverydifferentcoursesbasedonseeminglyirrelevantfactors,suchastheirfamilyrelationshipsortheireducationallevels.Inmypractice,thesickestpeopleIseeoftensharesimilarbackgrounds:loneliness,abuse,poverty,ordiscrimination.Forthem,themedicalmodelisn'tenough.It'slikefixingupanairplaneengineandignoringthatthepilotisonhisthirddrinkatthebarandamassivestormisoverhead...Toproperlycareforpatients,wealsoneedtocareaboutthelivesofthepeoplegettingthecare."K）在多处篇幅中，她讲述了那些遭遇"流水线式医疗"的男女的故事——在那里，病人大多被当作一块块肉。她写道："在临床上，常见两名患有相同病症（如心脏病发作后康复）的患者，因看似无关的因素（如家庭关系或受教育程度）而走向截然不同的病程。在我的诊疗中，所见最重的病人往往有着相似的背景：孤独、受虐、贫困或歧视。对他们而言，医疗模式并不足够。

sents.en: Factors like love, friendship, and dignity.
sents.cn: 这就像修好飞机引擎，却无视飞行员正在酒吧喝下第三杯酒、头顶正有猛烈风暴……要妥善照顾病人，我们也需要关心接受照护者的生活。

sents.en: There's a social dimension to health that we've completely overlooked in our efforts to find the best and most cutting-edge medical care...
